intro.name: The secret of life
intro.text:
(Subject) has spent years studying the mysteries of living things. (subject.He/she) knows how roots drink from the earth, how wounds mend, and how a tiny seed becomes a towering tree. Yet one question torments (subject.him/her): Why does life end, and could it ever be persuaded to return?
Lately, (Subject) has been gathering bones, clay, rawhide, dried herbs, and strange jars from the farthest corners of Isola. (subject.His/her) workshop is lit long after everyone else has gone to bed. At dawn, (Friend) discovers a carefully stitched animal-shaped figure lying beneath a sheet.

question.name: The figure
question.text:
"It is not what you think," says (Subject).
"I haven't said what I think," replies (Friend).
"Then please continue not thinking it."
(Subject) explains that (subject.he/she) intends to discover the secret of restoring life itself. (Friend) must decide what to do.

choices.label: Ask the healers and elders to investigate.
Ask (SUBJECT) what (subject.he/she) is really trying to bring back.

a1.name: A1
a1.text: At sunset, (Subject) unveils a motionless little creature resting on a bed of leaves. (subject.He/she) raises both hands and cries, "BEHOLD!" The creature suddenly opens its eyes, scrambles upright, and races out the door. The villagers scream. (Subject) begins weeping with triumph.

a1_2.name: A1
a1_2.text: Then the head healer examines the abandoned bed and announces that the creature had merely been sleeping. "So," asks a child, "you invented waking up?" (Subject) spends the rest of the evening insisting that this is still a significant discovery.

a2.name: A2
a2.text: The sheet comes off. Beneath it stands a figure of clay, bones, carved wood, and rawhide, held upright by a complicated arrangement of vines. "My creation will WALK!" (Subject) declares, pulling a cord. One leg rises.

a2_2.name: A2
a2_2.text: The entire figure topples forward and scatters across the floor. A small child begins applauding. "It walked once!" (Subject) shouts. "It fell," says (Friend). "All great journeys begin with a first step!" "That was its last step."

a3.name: A3
a3.text: (Subject) places a sealed pot before the gathering and announces that the substance inside has become alive. The pot bubbles ominously. An experienced farmer sniffs it and identifies a mixture of fermented fruit and yeast.

a4.name: A4
a4.text: The experiment fails, but one of the healers notices that (Subject)'s careful records show how different plant fibers hold a dressing together.

a4_2.name: A4
a4_2.text: The healers test the fibers safely and discover a useful way to bind splints. (Subject) is congratulated. "I set out to master the boundary between life and death," (subject.he/she) says grandly. "And instead," replies the healer, "you've helped someone keep a broken arm still. That is no small thing."

a5.name: A5
a5.text: (Subject) has built a tall frame covered in animal hide. At the decisive moment, (subject.he/she) pulls a vine, releasing a concealed stone weight. The frame shudders and emits a terrible groan. Half the audience flees. The other half stays long enough to see (Subject) emerge from behind the curtain, laughing. "IT MOVED!" (subject.he/she) cries. "You pulled it!" says (Friend). "YES! IT MOVED BECAUSE I PULLED IT!" Nobody is certain whether the experiment succeeded, failed, or was intended as a joke. (Subject) refuses to clarify.

text_only.reason: the audience runs from the room; nobody leaves the village

a6.name: A6
a6.text: The villagers watch as (Subject) carefully follows every step in (subject.his/her) notes. Nothing moves. Nothing breathes. Nothing changes. At last, (Subject) covers the figure again.

a6_2.name: A6
a6_2.text: "I was so certain," (subject.he/she) whispers. (Friend) helps clean the workshop without offering a clever remark. The following morning, (Subject) begins writing a new page: WHAT I LEARNED FROM BEING WRONG.

b1.name: B1
b1.text: "You cannot forbid the pursuit of knowledge!" (Subject) cries. (subject.He/she) throws a dramatic cloak over (subject.his/her) shoulders, announces the founding of THE GREAT HALL OF FORBIDDEN DISCOVERIES, and storms away. The cloak catches on the doorframe. (Subject) must return for it. "THIS CHANGES NOTHING!" (subject.he/she) declares. The villagers agree that it changes very little.

b2.name: B2
b2.text: (Friend) explains that curiosity is welcome, but taking shared supplies without permission and frightening the village are not.

b2_2.name: B2
b2_2.text: (Subject) argues, then reluctantly agrees to keep a proper inventory and demonstrate only harmless experiments in public. A week later, the workshop door bears a new sign: DO NOT ENTER UNLESS YOU HAVE A QUESTION WORTH ASKING. Someone adds beneath it: OR YOU ARE RETURNING OUR BOWLS.

b3.name: B3
b3.text: (Subject) agrees far too quickly. Soon, strange noises are heard from a shed behind the trees.

b3_2.name: B3
b3_2.text: (Friend) investigates and finds (Subject) surrounded by wooden birds, clay frogs, and a mechanical crab made of shells. "I said I would stop trying to bring the dead back," (Subject) says defensively.

b3_3.name: B3
b3_3.text: "I never promised to stop making things walk." The crab scuttles half an inch before falling over. (Friend) decides this is an improvement.

b4.name: B4
b4.text: The village laughs at (Subject)'s work, and a few people begin calling (subject.him/her) a fool. (Subject) quietly locks the workshop and stops attending research lessons. Days later, (Friend) finds a pile of torn notes beside the door.

b4_2.name: B4
b4_2.text: "You can tell me my idea is wrong," (Subject) says. "You needn't tell me I am worthless." (Friend) apologizes and invites (subject.him/her) to help with a smaller, safer project. It takes time before (Subject) agrees.

b5.name: B5
b5.text: (Subject) gathers the village and solemnly announces that (subject.he/she) is abandoning all foolish experiments. To prove it, (subject.he/she) throws a bundle of drawings into the fire. The drawings are damp and refuse to burn.

b5_2.name: B5
b5_2.text: (Subject) tries again. The fire goes out. A child observes that this may be (subject.his/her) most successful experiment yet: the discovery of a way to extinguish flames. (Subject) begins taking notes before anyone can stop (subject.him/her).

b6.name: B6
b6.text: (Subject) confesses that the experiments have consumed (subject.his/her) days and nights. "I thought if I worked hard enough, I could make the world obey me," (subject.he/she) says. The villagers help dismantle the dangerous parts of the workshop, leaving the books, tools, and harmless models intact. (Subject) returns to ordinary work. Sometimes (subject.he/she) still watches the stars with an expression nobody can quite read.

c1.name: C1
c1.text: The healers examine every jar, drawing, and specimen. At last, the eldest speaks. "Your observations are careful. Your conclusions are not." (Subject) looks wounded.

c1_2.name: C1
c1_2.text: "You have not found a way to return life," the healer continues, "but you have found many questions worth studying properly." (Subject) agrees to work alongside the healers. (subject.He/she) insists on keeping the enormous handwritten title THE SECRET OF LIFE above the desk.

c2.name: C2
c2.text: The investigation reveals that several bones used in the figure came from an old communal teaching collection. (Subject) insists (subject.he/she) meant to return them. "After your creation walked away?" asks (Friend). "Naturally."

c2_2.name: C2
c2_2.text: The elders order the collection restored and ask (Subject) to apologize to the teacher who had been searching for it. (Subject) does so, although (subject.he/she) continues to describe the matter as a regrettable misunderstanding between two great minds.

c3.name: C3
c3.text: A healer discovers that (Subject) has combined unfamiliar plants in a sealed jar. Rather than opening it near the crowd, the healers isolate the jar and safely dispose of the mixture. (Subject) is furious at first, then ashamed when (subject.he/she) realizes how little (subject.he/she) knew about its contents. "I wanted to discover something extraordinary," (subject.he/she) admits. "Then begin by learning what you already have," the healer replies.

c4.name: C4
c4.text: The elders hold a public discussion on whether a discovery is valuable simply because it is possible.

c4_2.name: C4
c4_2.text: The farmers argue about resources, the healers about care, the researchers about freedom, and the children about whether the clay creature would need to eat.

c4_3.name: C4
c4_3.text: By sunset, no one agrees on the meaning of life, but everyone agrees that (Subject) must stop borrowing bowls without asking. The meeting is declared a partial success.

c5.name: C5
c5.text: A healer gently asks why (Subject) is so determined to reverse death. (Subject) tries to explain the experiments, the measurements, the drawings. Finally, (subject.he/she) stops. "Because I miss someone," (subject.he/she) says. The workshop falls silent. The healer sits beside (subject.him/her). No grand discovery is made that evening, but for the first time in months, (Subject) does not sit alone.

c6.name: C6
c6.text: One of the investigators accidentally knocks a wooden arm on the floor. It springs upright, strikes a hanging bell, and startles everyone. (Subject) leaps to (subject.his/her) feet. "YOU SEE? IT LIVES!"

c6_2.name: C6
c6_2.text: The builder examines the arm and discovers an ingenious tensioned-vine mechanism. "It doesn't live," the builder says, "but it could lift water." (Subject) is offered help adapting the mechanism. (subject.He/she) accepts, after demanding that the water-lifter be named THE AWAKENING.

c7.name: C7
c7.text: The elders determine that no law has been broken, but the experiment has frightened the village. They ask (Subject) to explain the work honestly and listen to the objections. (Subject) does both, with visible difficulty. The elders allow harmless research to continue. The question that started it all remains unanswered, and (Subject) must learn to live with that.

d1.name: D1
d1.text: (Subject) looks at the stitched figure for a long time. "There used to be someone who asked me what I was studying every morning," (subject.he/she) says. "Now nobody does." (Friend) does not pretend to have an answer. Instead, (friend.he/she) offers to visit the workshop each morning and ask about the day's work. It is a small promise, but (Subject) accepts it.

d2.name: D2
d2.text: "I am afraid," (Subject) admits. "One day everything I have learned will disappear with me." (Friend) suggests teaching the younger researchers. (Subject) objects that the children will ask foolish questions.

d2_2.name: D2
d2_2.text: "Then you'll have plenty in common," (Friend) replies. The next week, (Subject) begins a lesson on living things. It is interrupted by seventeen questions and one frog. (Subject) enjoys it more than expected.

d3.name: D3
d3.text: (Subject) explains that (subject.he/she) once promised a loved one to discover why living things die. The promise became an obsession. (Friend) asks whether the loved one would have wanted (subject.him/her) to stop living in order to keep it. (Subject) cannot answer immediately. That evening, (subject.he/she) closes the workshop early and joins the village meal.

d4.name: D4
d4.text: "Nobody," (Subject) replies, genuinely puzzled. "I simply wanted to know whether it could be done." (Friend) stares at the clay figure. "You spent six months building a dead goat out of sticks because you were curious?"

d4_2.name: D4
d4_2.text: "It is not a goat," (Subject) replies indignantly. "It is a prototype." "A prototype of what?" (Subject) opens (subject.his/her) mouth, then closes it. For the first time, (subject.he/she) realizes the question deserves an answer.

d5.name: D5
d5.text: (Subject) proudly reveals that (subject.he/she) has been trying to create a creature that will do all the village's chores. "Then why give it claws?" (Friend) asks. "For gathering fruit." "And teeth?"

d5_2.name: D5
d5_2.text: "For cracking coconuts." "And three heads?" "TO MULTIPLY ITS EFFICIENCY!" (Friend) quietly suggests that a basket and two willing workers might be more practical. (Subject) accuses (friend.him/her) of lacking vision.

d6.name: D6
d6.text: (Subject) confesses that (subject.he/she) wanted to do something no one else had ever done. (Friend) reminds (subject.him/her) that discoveries need not be grand to matter.

d6_2.name: D6
d6_2.text: Months later, (Subject) finishes a careful guide to the plants and animals of Isola. A child reads the first page and asks a question that (Subject) cannot answer. (subject.He/she) smiles. "Excellent. We shall find out."

a3_2_food.name: A3
a3_2_food.text: "Then why is it moving?" (Subject) demands. "Because it's fermenting," the farmer replies. (Subject) considers this for a long time. "Then I have not conquered death," (subject.he/she) admits, "but I may have improved our bread."
